title: Security tool registry (manifests/security-tools.json)
description: The tool registry bin/audit.mjs runs. WRITTEN 2026-08-25 against the 13 entries that existed, because the data file had declared `$schema: ../schema/tools.schema.json` for its whole life and that file did not exist — so it advertised a contract nobody could check, and a reader took the pointer's presence as evidence it was validated. Every field below is REQUIRED because every field is present on all 13 entries: the schema is derived from the artifact rather than from an intention about it, which is the only way it can be true on the day it is written. `isolation` is the sole optional key (2 of 13). Adding a genuinely optional field later is a deliberate edit here; that is the point.

gates.description: gate id -> human description of the precondition it names. A tool's `gate` must resolve here; an unresolvable gate is a tool that can never run and never says why.

id.description: Stable identifier. Reaches the filesystem and the report tree, so it is constrained at the source rather than sanitised downstream.

gate.description: The precondition this tool needs. May be a compound (`openapi+running-app`); each component must appear in `gates`.

rationale.description: WHY this tool and not the adjacent one. A registry of tools without rationales becomes a list nobody can prune, because no entry says what would make it redundant.

report.description: Artifact the run writes. bin/audit.mjs records `noscan` when this is missing or unparseable — never 'ran, no findings'.

dependsOn.description: Other tool ids. Topo-sorted into the remediation DAG; a cycle or an unknown id is a registry defect, not a runtime one.

isolation.description: Optional. Present on 2 of 13 at time of writing.
